scientific_role: Minimal topology-aware analytic baseline from already-fixed I1 provider cards. M0 composes local LCQ boundaries forward through G, reads every provider card at rho_i=rho_G, and multiplies the corresponding local sigma values under its independence model. It is a predictor/baseline, not a guaranteed certificate for the global rho_G query.

allowed: exogenous global admissibility query A_G and rho_G
deterministic fixed-stage and network boundary terms
forbidden: redistributing or optimizing rho_G across providers

global_query_relation: Compose the already-fixed local A_i boundaries forward through G. M0 is applicable to an exogenous A_G only when the induced boundary is contained in A_G: l_M0<=l_G, c_M0<=c_G, q_M0>=q_G.

rho_policy.rationale: M0 deliberately uses the most direct local reading of the I1 cards. It does not engineer local tolerances to preserve the global violation fraction. Any error caused by this simplification is part of the baseline limitation being measured.

probability_composition.interpretation: analytic prediction/baseline for the global admissibility probability, not a lower bound or certification guarantee

known_limitation.statement: Even if c_i>=rho_G for every provider, this does not in general imply c_G>=rho_G for an all-required composition. For m providers, the union of local violation sets can be as large as m(1-rho_G). M0 intentionally does not correct this by allocating a tighter local violation budget.
known_limitation.scientific_role: This is a deliberate borderline limitation of M0 and motivates richer integration methods such as M1.

hard_preconditions_for_numeric_predictio: forward-composed fixed A_i boundary is contained in the requested A_G
the requested H point exists in every required I1 card
the requested rho_G slice exists in every required I1 card
failure_semantics: If a required boundary or card point is unavailable, M0 reports NOT_APPLICABLE rather than changing Phase 2, interpolating an unexposed rho, or redistributing rho_G.
evaluation_lock: The same-rho M0 rule is frozen before M0 is compared with any Phase-1 white-box sigma outcome.
